summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain and critically high blood glucose, found to be due to insulin pump discontinuation and possible infection. She had a history of chronic pancreatitis and gastroparesis, with new right-sided abdominal pain. Initial concerns for biliary obstruction were ruled out by a limited RUQ ultrasound showing no acute process, though fatty liver was noted. Hyperglycemia resolved with IV insulin and transition to scheduled Lantus, with discontinuation of the non-prescribed insulin pump. Pain was managed with home Dilaudid regimen per narcotics agreement. Urine culture showed contamination, and antibiotics were discontinued. Chest tightness improved without intervention. The patient declined inpatient MRCP with secretin and will follow up as an outpatient. She was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating diet, with plans for chest CT follow-up in three months.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
